subject: Executive briefing: sustained service variance & proposed remedies
messages:
From: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Torres <s.torres@finica.com>, procurement@finica.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency & increased error rate since pool migration

Aditya,

We started seeing a noticeable uptick in tail latency and a 3.7% increase in 5xx errors for our production routes since the Dedicated pool switchover on Tuesday. This is impacting our user flows during peak hours — query times that were ~300ms are spiking to 1.2s and the frontend is surfacing retries. Our SREs gathered request samples and attached a short log.

We need:
- Immediate mitigation steps and an ETA for stabilization
- An accounting of SLA exposure and proposed credit amount
- A plan to prevent recurrence (permanent fix + validation steps)

I’m escalating this to our procurement and will need an official position from Redwood for our exec review.

Thanks,
Carolyn Park
VP Product, Finica

Attachment: service-impact-log.txt (10KB)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & increased error rate since pool migration

Hi Carolyn — thank you for the heads up and the log. I’m really sorry for the disruption; this falls short of the experience we aim to deliver.

Quick updates:
- I’ve opened an incident (RID-2461) and our infra team is reverting a recent kernel parameter change on the Dedicated pool that correlates with the rollout window. We expect preliminary improvement within 60–90 minutes.
- I’m attaching a short SLO impact spreadsheet so we can converge on exposure numbers. (slo-analysis.xlsx)
- I’ll loop in our head of customer success and ops for a remediation and credit proposal — we’ll aim to get a formal reply today.

I’ll keep you posted every 30 minutes until the spike is resolved.

— Aditya
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & increased error rate since pool migration

Carolyn — Marissa here (Account Exec). Apologies for the disruption. We’re tracking the incident and have two parallel workstreams: short-term mitigation (revert/config tuning) and a postmortem with root cause and test cases.

Next steps from our side:
- Confirmed: temporary revert completed; infra saw 40% drop in 5xx in the first 30 minutes.
- Ops will run a 24-hour soak with increased telemetry across Finica routes.
- We’ll present a proposed service variance credit (calculated against the impacted hourly windows) and a MAP (mutual action plan) for validation testing by Monday.

Can you confirm who from Finica will be on the Monday validation call? Sam? procurement?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@finica.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>, procurement@finica.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency & increased error rate since pool migration

Thanks for the quick action. To be frank, Carolyn and I need the credit calculation to be explicit — our finance team is asking for the dollar value and the contract amendment language for SLA definitions. Given this is outside typical operational noise, our CFO will review any proposed remediation or credit.

Please escalate to leadership if you need sign-off beyond standard account credits.

— Sam
Director, Platform Engineering, Finica
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@finica.com>, Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed service-variance credit & MAP (draft)

Team — attaching our draft credit calculation and MAP summary (proposed-credit-calculation.pdf). High level:
- Impact window: 2026-05-19 22:00 UTC through 2026-05-20 06:00 UTC (eight hour window with elevated tail latency and 5xxs)
- Measured SLA exposure: 5.1% of billed inference units for that window (per SLO metrics)
- Proposed remedy: one-time credit equal to 60% of the prorated usage during impacted hours (not to exceed three months of committed capacity credits), plus engineering hours for validation testing at no charge.

We want to be pragmatic: if Finica prefers a straight dollar credit, we can compute that from your committed monthly spend. Alternatively, we can amend the contract to clarify SLO definitions and monitoring hooks and replace the credit with a multi-month service credit.

Can Laura and Sean confirm operational approval for the 60% credit cap? I’m happy to sync with Finica’s CFO for numbers.

— Aditya
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@finica.com>, Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed service-variance credit & MAP (draft)

Sam, Carolyn — Laura here (Head of Revenue Operations). After reviewing the incident and our risk exposure, Redwood can confirm operational approval for the one-time credit described below:
- Credit: 60% of prorated usage during the impacted eight-hour window, applied as a usage credit to Finica’s account within the next billing cycle.
- Cap: The credit will not exceed the equivalent of three months’ committed capacity credits under the existing agreement.
- Contract amendment: We will propose a succinct SLA clarification (SLO thresholds, alert hooks, and remediation timelines). Draft language will be sent via DocuSign for review.

We’ll also commit to a joint validation run (Monday 2026-06-01) to verify stability and to a 30-day telemetry review. Our legal and procurement teams are ready to coordinate redlines.

Attachment: proposed-credit-calculation.pdf

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@finica.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@finica.com>, procurement@finica.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed service-variance credit & MAP (draft)

Laura, Aditya — thanks for the clear proposal and for moving quickly. Finica accepts the 60% prorated usage credit applied to the next billing cycle with the stated cap, contingent on:
1) Receipt of the DocuSign for the SLA clarification by EOD Monday (2026-05-31)
2) A joint validation call on 2026-06-01 with the Finica SREs
3) A follow-up telemetry review after 30 days with a shared dashboard and access to the incident logs used for calculations.

Procurement will coordinate the DocuSign review. Once we have the signed amendment we will mark this as resolved from our side.

— Sam
Director, Platform Engineering, Finica
